messages:
sara: Heads-up — got an escalated ticket from ACME about a large jump in p95/p99 for text-gen on the gpt-medium3 family since last night. They attached traces showing slow attention kernels. p95 went from ~120ms to ~560ms, p99 to ~1.2s. Happened right after the runtime compile flags were flipped in canary (FlashAttention preferred).

cheng: thanks — seeing same in our dashboards for region us-east-1. Alerting spike at ~2026-03-14T22:08:00Z. Query: did we change SDPA -> FlashAttention default in the kernel selector?

deploy-bot: canary deploy finished: commit bf3a7e2 -> runtime-canary-2026-03-14. Flags: `-DFLASH_ATTN=1 -O3 -march=native`. Targets: gw-22, gw-23 (10% traffic).

maya (oncall): I pulled a couple of traces. The KV cache hit path seems fine, but attention kernel time increased a lot for sequence lengths ~1024. CPU tail not high, GPU occupancy looks ok. Might be a pathological code path in FlashAttention for this model shape.

alex: Do we have reproducible repro? If we can reproduce locally we can toggle the kernel and test.

sara: Support provided a small repro curl that hits their route:  
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-medium3","input":"Q: Summarize...","max_tokens":256,"stream":false}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
They said running 50 concurrent clients yields the same p95 jump.

cheng: On a staging gw with the canary flags I ran a focused bench: 50 concurrent execs, seq=1024, batch size 1. FlashAttention kernel avg token latency increased 4x compared to SDPA selected build. I can paste flamegraphs.

infra-bot: gpu nodes gw-22 and gw-23 show increased kernel time for `attn_flashforward` and more L2 traffic. Memory access pattern looks different.

maya (oncall): Quick mitigation options: 1) revert canary (full rollback) 2) change kernel selector to prefer SDPA for gpt-medium3 shapes 3) add runtime flag to force `REDWOOD_KERNEL_PREF=sdpa,flash` so customers can opt out. Which do we want?

alex: For a high-severity customer impact we should rollback the canary to be safe. But also add an immediate runtime override so we can keep the new build canaryed for perf testing on other shapes.

sara: Support-bot asked for ETA to keep customer updated. They need repro steps + what mitigations we've applied.

cheng: I can push a targeted kernel-selector hotfix to the canary hosts that sets preference by model/seq. Patch looks like:  
```
// kernel_selector.cpp
if (model == "gpt-medium3" && seq >= 512) {
  return Kernel::SDPA;
}
```
Will test on gw-22 only first.

deploy-bot: starting hotpatch job: hotpatch/ker-sel-1778 -> gw-22 (1 host)

maya (oncall): While that's running, we should prepare a full rollback plan in case hotpatch fails. Alex can you open a rollback ticket?

alex: Opening rollback ticket now. Quick note: we should snapshot the canary metrics so we can compare. Also add a compile-flag toggle endpoint to flip `FLASH_ATTN` at runtime (shorter term).

cheng: Hotpatch applied to gw-22. Preliminary bench: p95 back down to ~150ms, p99 ~300ms on that host. gw-23 still high.

support-bot: replied to customer: "we identified an attention kernel regression tied to a canary compile flag. We are applying a targeted fix and will roll back fully if the fix doesn't stabilize p95/p99 in the next 60 min. Thanks for repro steps, keep them coming."

infra-bot: Started canary rollback plan to remove runtime-canary-2026-03-14 from gw-23.

alex: Rollback in flight. Meanwhile, I'm preparing an A/B test config: prefer SDPA for seq >= 512 by default in the selector service. We'll wire that to a feature flag `feat.kernel.pref.sdpa` so we can toggle quickly.

maya (oncall): Postmortem action items we should capture now: - add unit regression tests for commonly-seen seq lengths (256,512,1024) that run both FlashAttention and SDPA kernels and compare latency distribution - add a toggle in the operator console to force kernel selection per-model - add performance gating in canary (p95 delta threshold)

cheng: Confirming repro script used: 
```
# repro.py
import requests, time
URL = 'https://canary-gw-22.internal/v1/generate'
hdr = { 'Authorization': 'Bearer test', 'Content-Type':'application/json' }
for i in range(1000):
    t0 = time.time()
    r = requests.post(URL, json={"model":"gpt-medium3","input":"x"*800,"max_tokens":128}, headers=hdr)
    print(i, r.status_code, round((time.time()-t0)*1000,1))
```
Use concurrency with multiple processes to reproduce p95/p99.

cheng: Also validated that forcing env `REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=sdpa` at process start yields stable low latency. So as emergency mitigation we can set that on the remaining canary hosts.

deploy-bot: gw-23 env updated: `REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=sdpa`. Restarting runtime process.

infra-bot: gw-23 restarted, health checks green. Post-change bench shows p95 ~160ms, p99 ~340ms.

sara: Great — pleased to report customer confirmed latency dropped and they've paused escalation. They want a short writeup of root cause and follow-ups.

maya (oncall): Root cause (working summary): a compile-time FlashAttention optimization exposed a regression for certain sequence lengths on our GPU kernel variant, causing worse memory access pattern and increased L2 traffic. The kernel selector defaulted to FlashAttention in canary, affecting 10% of traffic. Mitigation: hotpatch selector rules + env override + rollback to stable on remaining hosts while we run targeted perf tests.

alex: Follow-ups to assign: 1) perf regression test suite (cheng) 2) kernel selector feature flag + console control (alex) 3) investigate FlashAttention codepath and file bug with upstream (cheng + runtime-ml) 4) update canary gating to include p95/p99 thresholds (maya).

cheng: I'll upload collected flamegraphs and L2 counters to the eng-runtime drive and post link here after a quick scrub.

support-bot: closing escalation ticket with status: mitigated. Customer follow-up scheduled in 24h.

sara: Thanks all. One note for the writeup: include exact commits, canary host IDs, and the repro snippet so customer can rerun if needed. I'll draft and circulate.
